24	MINCHECKS=${MINCHECKS:-15}
25	# SKIPCI=1 during an Actions outage: CI can never go green, and a CodeRabbit slot
26	# expires whether or not it is used, so waiting for CI throws the slot away.
27	[ "${SKIPCI:-0}" = "1" ] && echo "SKIPCI=1 - not gating on CI (Actions outage)"
28	for i in $(seq 1 30); do
29	  [ "${SKIPCI:-0}" = "1" ] && break
30	  sleep 20
31	  FAIL=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE" or .conclusion=="TIMED_OUT")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
32	  PEND=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion==null)|select((.name // .context)|test("CodeRabbit|Macroscope";"i")|not)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
33	  OK=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="SUCCESS")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
34	  DONE=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion!=null)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
35	  echo "[$(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)] ci: success=$OK settled=$DONE pending=$PEND failed=$FAIL (need >=$MINCHECKS)"
36	  if [ -n "$FAIL" ] && [ "$FAIL" != "0" ]; then
37	    echo "CI FAILED on $HEAD - not flipping"
38	    $GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE")|.name'
39	    exit 4
40	  fi
41	  if [ "$PEND" = "0" ] && [ -n "$PEND" ] && { [ -n "$DONE" ] && [ "$DONE" -ge "$MINCHECKS" ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
42	    echo "CI GREEN ($DONE checks settled)"; break
43	  fi
44	  sleep 40
45	done
46	
47	# 2. Respect the CodeRabbit hourly reset.
48	NOW=$(date -u +%s)
49	if [ "$NOTBEFORE" -gt "$NOW" ]; then
50	  echo "waiting $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))s for the review slot"; sleep $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))
51	fi
52	
53	BASE=""
54	for a in 1 2 3; do
55	  BASE=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"' 2>/dev/null)
56	  [ -n "$BASE" ] && break
57	  echo "  baseline read failed (attempt $a) - retrying"; sleep 15
58	done
59	[ -n "$BASE" ] || { echo "CANNOT READ CR BASELINE - aborting before flipping"; exit 6; }
60	echo "baseline cr status-comment updated_at=$BASE"
61	
62	# Flip must be CONFIRMED. A swallowed `gh pr ready` failure (network) leaves the PR
63	# a draft while the poll loop below waits out its full timeout on verdicts that can
64	# never arrive - which reads as "no findings" when nothing was ever reviewed.
65	FLIPPED=0
66	for a in 1 2 3 4 5; do
67	  $GH pr ready $PR >/dev/null 2>&1
68	  sleep 5
69	  D=$($GH pr view $PR --json isDraft --jq '.isDraft' 2>/dev/null)
70	  if [ "$D" = "false" ]; then FLIPPED=1; echo "FLIPPED READY $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"; break; fi
71	  echo "  flip attempt $a did not take (isDraft=[$D]) - retrying"
72	  sleep 20
73	done
74	[ "$FLIPPED" = "1" ] || { echo "COULD NOT FLIP #$PR READY - aborting. No review slot was consumed."; exit 5; }
75	
76	# 3. Hold ready until BOTH verdicts are on THIS head, or 40m.
77	#    CR verdict  == a body-bearing review whose commit_id is the head.
78	#    macroscope  == its check-runs exist on the head and none are still in flight.
79	CR_DONE=0; MS_DONE=0; MS_REVIEWED=0
80	for i in $(seq 1 40); do
81	  sleep 60
82	  U_NOW=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
83	  if [ "$CR_DONE" = "0" ]; then
84	    # gh api takes no --arg, so the head is interpolated into the filter.
85	    N=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq "[.[]|select(.user.login|test(\"coderabbit\";\"i\"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==\"$HEAD\")]|length" 2>/dev/null)
86	    # A CLEAN verdict posts NO review — it only edits the status comment. Findings
87	    # come as a review body; both surfaces have to be polled.
88	    CLEAN=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("No actionable comments";"i"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
89	    if { [ -n "$N" ] && [ "$N" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
90	      CR_DONE=1; echo "  CR VERDICT (findings) on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"
91	    elif { [ -n "$CLEAN" ] && [ "$CLEAN" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null && [ -n "$U_NOW" ] && [ "$U_NOW" != "$BASE" ]; then
92	      CR_DONE=1; echo "  CR VERDICT (clean, status comment) @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"
93	    fi
94	  fi
95	  if [ "$MS_DONE" = "0" ]; then
96	    MST=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
97	    MSP=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|select(.status!="completed")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
98	    # "completed" is not "reviewed": a skipped run completes too. Out of credits,
99	    # macroscope skips all five with "Credit balance exhausted", which the old
100	    # completed-count test scored as full coverage.
101	    MSR=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|select(.conclusion!="skipped")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
102	    MSX=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|select((.output.title // "")|test("[Cc]redit balance exhausted"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
103	    if { [ -n "$MSX" ] && [ "$MSX" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
104	      MS_DONE=1; MS_REVIEWED=0
105	      echo "  MACROSCOPE OUT OF CREDITS on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ) - NOT REVIEWED, not waiting"
106	    elif [ -n "$MST" ] && [ "$MST" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && [ "$MSP" = "0" ]; then
107	      MS_DONE=1
108	      if { [ -n "$MSR" ] && [ "$MSR" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
109	        MS_REVIEWED=1; echo "  MACROSCOPE REVIEWED on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ) ($MSR of $MST agents ran)"
110	      else
111	        MS_REVIEWED=0; echo "  MACROSCOPE ALL SKIPPED on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ) - NOT REVIEWED"
112	      fi
113	    fi
114	  fi
115	  LIM=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("Review limit reached";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // ""' 2>/dev/null)
116	  echo "  t+${i}m cr_done=$CR_DONE ms_done=$MS_DONE cr_comment_upd=$U_NOW ratelimit=[$LIM]"
117	  [ "$CR_DONE" = "1" ] && [ "$MS_DONE" = "1" ] && break
118	done

121	for a in 1 2 3 4; do
122	  $GH pr ready $PR --undo >/dev/null 2>&1
123	  sleep 5
124	  D=$($GH pr view $PR --json isDraft --jq '.isDraft' 2>/dev/null)

126	  echo "  re-draft attempt $a did not take (isDraft=[$D]) - retrying"; sleep 15
127	  [ "$a" = "4" ] && echo "WARNING: #$PR MAY STILL BE READY - re-draft it by hand"

137	echo "-- coverage --"

139	[ "$MS_REVIEWED" = "1" ] || echo "WARNING: macroscope did NOT review this head. CodeRabbit is the only bot verdict."
140	[ "$CR_DONE" = "1" ] && [ "$MS_DONE" = "1" ] && exit 0

content.text:
**#1147 is clean and back to draft. Nothing to fix.**

CodeRabbit posted "No actionable comments were generated" and — the part worth checking — its comment cites the commit range `d11bfce11...b093f7c56` and all 6 files, so it genuinely reviewed this head rather than a stale one. Zero review threads, zero inline comments.

**Two things the run told us about coverage, and neither is good news:**

**Macroscope is still out of credits.** It ran all five agents and skipped all five with "Credit balance exhausted". The script caught this correctly and did not wait — and importantly, it scores this as `macroscope_reviewed=0`, not as coverage. A `completed` check-run that was skipped is exactly the false all-clear this repo has been bitten by before.

**Greptile did not review, and it did not review #1141 either.** The only reviewers on the last merged PR were CodeRabbit and you. So my earlier statement that "Greptile has no cap and will review all of them regardless" was wrong — Greptile appears to be inactive on this repo right now. That matters for the queue: **CodeRabbit is currently the only bot verdict on every one of these eight PRs.** Worth knowing before #1156 and #1158, the two large security-sensitive ones.

A transient GitHub API failure also hit one of my verification calls. I re-ran it with retries rather than letting a failed query read as "no findings" — the state above is from a confirmed successful response.

The hourly slot is now spent; it resets around **16:15Z**. Next in merge order is **#1151**, the facade shape change that everything else rebases onto.

Given Greptile is absent and macroscope is dry, do you want me to keep the queue purely on CodeRabbit, or should I put an independent review sub-agent on the two big ones — #1156, the FUSE write path with plaintext at rest, and #1158, prune — while we wait out the hourly resets? Those cost nothing against the CodeRabbit limit and would run in parallel with the queue.

**#1157 came back with 2 nitpicks, both in `crates/engine/tests/net.rs`** — and one of them is worth taking seriously rather than dismissing as a nit.

The first is a straight hit against this repo's own comment law: the doc comments on `assert_no_endpoint_holds` and `head_value_at` restate what the helpers do rather than why they exist.

The second is a genuine coverage gap. `revive` selects the fan-out record when its sequence **equals** the recovery sequence — that tie-break at `>=` was a deliberate design decision, because a same-sequence fork is expected after an unconfirmed publish retry. Nothing tests it. That is exactly the case where a stale CID could ride a corroborated sequence, which is the defect the PR exists to prevent.

**#1151's full web review: 1 actionable comment, and it is a fair one.**

The doc on `CommandOutcome` read "What a command handed back across the worker boundary" — an incomplete sentence that describes what the type does rather than telling a host anything useful.

I did not take CodeRabbit's proposed replacement ("Hosts need a discriminated result to handle each command outcome"), because that is just a different "what" sentence and does not match how this file documents anything else. Instead I matched the file's own convention: `Event` has the identical `kind`-plus-payload-getter shape and reads "One event the engine emits… Read `kind`, then the matching payload getter." So `CommandOutcome` now reads:

> The result of one `Engine::command` call. Read `kind`, then the matching payload getter.

That tells a host the actual access pattern, which is the thing worth knowing.

Gates are running on the change.

**One thing I noticed but did not fix, because it is outside the finding.** `CommandOutcome` is placed directly under the `// Snapshot read surface — key-free view state projected by the engine` banner, but a command result is not snapshot read surface. The PR introduced the type there. Moving it above that banner would be a two-line change and would stop the section header from being wrong. Say the word and I will fold it into the same commit; otherwise I leave it, since expanding scope on a review fix is how the unrelated-churn problems start.

The bigger takeaway from this round: the CLI said 0 findings on this exact commit and the full web review found 1. Same head, same files. That is the under-reporting gap measured directly, and it is why I would not let the CLI stand in for a web verdict on #1156 or #1158.

input.content:
---
name: feedback-never-write-a-closing-keyword-to-negate-it
description: "Writing 'Does not close #NNNN' in a PR body still auto-closes the issue — GitHub's parser ignores the negation"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
---

**Never put a closing keyword next to an issue number in a PR body to say the opposite.**

On 2026-08-07 I edited PR #1151 to stop it closing #1016, replacing `Closes #1016` with the sentence
"Does **not** close #1016." GitHub's linked-issue parser matches `close|closes|closed|fix|fixes|
fixed|resolve|resolves|resolved` followed by `#N` **anywhere in the body and ignores the negation**,
so the merge closed #1016 anyway — while five open blockers remained on it. The exact phrasing meant
to prevent the close is what caused it.

**How to apply:** to reference an issue a PR does *not* close, rephrase so no keyword touches the
number — "the remaining arms are tracked in #1016", "see #1016" — or escape the reference. Then
**verify after the merge** that the issue is still open; the failure is silent and only shows up as a
wrongly-closed tracker item, which in turn falsely unblocks everything downstream of it (#1167 lost
its blocker until #1016 was reopened).

Same family as [[feedback-closes-vs-part-of-issue-hygiene]]: the tracker graph is only as honest as
the keywords in the PR body, and a wrong one fails toward "done".

The ordering is not cargo-cult — the two are separate ordered seam messages, and a kernel that learns the new size while still holding pre-commit pages serves them as the new version, including across a range a grown size just made valid. Data-first makes the intermediate state a short read, not a stale one; the test asserts the order.

I deliberately did *not* also clear `self.streamed` on commit — a stale entry there can only cause an extra invalidation, never a missed one.

**#1156's findings are all handled, head `2ace6f603`.** The Major fix is one line — `self.adapter.invalidate(Invalidation::Data { ino })` — plus the tests that prove it.

The verification behind it is what makes it trustworthy. The agent confirmed `Invalidation::Data` has exactly one other producer, `stream_for`, which fires only at *bind* time when the resolved `contentCid` differs from `streamed` — and a handle that already has a stream returns early and never reaches it. So nothing on the commit path repainted data at all. The new test fails without the fix with a precise message: `a commit must drop the pages of the version it replaced, got [Attributes { ino: 2 }]`.

It also justified the ordering rather than copying it: data-first matters because a kernel that learns the new size while still holding pre-commit pages will serve them *as* the new version, including across a range that a grown size just made valid. Data-first turns that into a short read instead of a stale one, and the test asserts the order.

**On finding 5, the agent corrected my reasoning, and it was right to.** I had suggested `ChunkCache` might mix versions; in fact it is keyed by `(StreamHandle, index)` and a stream pins one head version for its life, so that risk does not exist. But it found a better reason to defer: `version_block` clamps and zero-fills using per-handle `Pending` state, so caching the padded block under `(stream, index)` would poison reads for any other handle sharing that stream — re-introducing precisely what this branch's *previous* commit fixed. Filed as **#1168**, and for the first time this session a follow-up issue arrived correctly formed on the first attempt: `comp:desktop`, milestone, parent #991, `blocked_by` #1110, all verified.

All four gates green, 65 fuse-op tests passing, three threads replied to and resolved, nitpicks answered in a PR comment.

**One judgement call for you.** Unlike #1157, this fix changed production code, not just tests and comments — so my "skip the re-review" rule does not automatically apply. It is a single line that does exactly what the reviewer asked, with a failing-test proof. I would still skip the re-review and spend the next slot on #1149, but this is closer to the line than #1157 was. Say if you want it re-reviewed.

That fits, and it confirms the correction rather than complicating it. Marking #1156 ready in order to merge it triggered a CodeRabbit review attempt at ~21:22Z, which was refused — and the refusal reported 26 minutes remaining, putting the reset at ~21:48Z. That is exactly 60 minutes after #1156's review **started** at 20:48:34, not 60 minutes after its verdict at 20:55:52. So the window is start-based, as the reschedule assumes.

Two practical consequences:

The refusal cost nothing — a rejected attempt does not consume a slot, so 21:50 is genuinely clear for #1149.

And flipping a draft to ready purely to merge it will provoke a review attempt every time. Harmless when the limit refuses it, but if a slot happens to be free at that moment it would spend it on a PR you are about to merge. For #1158, #1145 and #1146, the safe order is to let the cycle review and re-draft first, then flip and merge — which is what we have been doing.

  [ $((i % 12)) -eq 0 ] && echo "[$(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)] waiting on github (probe $i, streak=$streak)"

## The defect

`hosted_quota_pre_flight` reconciles the account's BYO flag once per session:

```rust
if !self.byo_reconciled.get()
    && quota.advisory == hosted_leg
    && api.set_byo(!hosted_leg).await.is_ok()
```

It returns early on `Err(refusal)`, so only a placement that *resolved* reaches this line. After #1084 the only degraded placement that resolves is `DefaultsReason::UnprovenFirstRun` — the assumed first-run default, which is `Placement::Hosted`, so `hosted_leg = true`.

Chain:

1. Device A picks `External` and publishes. Its first write reconciles `advisory=false == hosted_leg=false` and PATCHes `byo=true`. The account flag is now true.
2. Device B is a fresh install on the same account. An adversary who controls the record-plane leg withholds the settings record. B holds none of the durable marks #1084 added, so the load reports `UnprovenFirstRun` and the placement is the assumed `Hosted`.
3. B's first write sees `advisory=true == hosted_leg=true` and PATCHes `byo=false`.

`Cargo Check & Test (Windows)` — a **required** context — can fail with:

```
error: linking with `link.exe` failed: exit code: 1104
error: could not compile `cipherbox-core` (example "kat_gen") due to 1 previous error
```

Seen 2026-08-07 on PR #1149 at head `4b8d1246a`. Exit 1104 from `link.exe` is a runner
resource/file-access failure, not a code defect. A plain re-run of the failed job went green with no
change to the diff.

**How to tell it apart from a real break, before touching the diff:** check whether the same job
passed on the PR's *previous* head. On #1149 the two new commits were a test assertion and a markdown
trim — neither can affect linking a `cipherbox-core` example — and `52dce2085` had Windows green.
That comparison is the cheap disambiguation; do it first.

**Gotcha:** `gh run rerun <id> --failed` is refused while the overall run is still `in_progress`
("cannot be rerun; its workflow file may be broken" — a misleading message). One Windows job can be
`completed/failure` while sibling jobs still run. Wait for the run to reach `completed`, then re-run.

Second known flaky required check alongside
[[project-web-e2e-smoke-signout-test-flaky]]. Re-run before triaging either.

**#1149 merged** — main is at `8c69c17c7`, **#1084 is closed**, and **#1159 is now fully unblocked** with no remaining blockers.

**The `write_plane.rs` conflict landed in #1158's rebase exactly as planned, and it was worth being careful about.** My first resolve looked plausible and was wrong — it left the settings test unterminated, because the conflict has *two* shared regions, not one. Git treated both the four-line test preamble and the trailing `);` `}` as common context, so each side was split across the other. Both had to be duplicated, once per side.

I aborted rather than patching the bad resolve, reset to the origin ref, and redid it with assertions on every boundary. The result: both tests present exactly once, each closing properly, all 8 commits replayed including the 4 banked from #1115.

That is why the gates matter here more than on any other rebase this wave — a hand-resolved conflict in a test file can compile and still silently drop a test. I am checking not just that the suite passes, but that **both** previously-conflicted tests actually appear in the run output.

Once green I will push, let CI settle, and run #1158's cycle on the next slot.

Found by the CodeRabbit gate on #1158 and confirmed against the branch at `319341e36`. Filed rather than fixed in that PR: the obvious fix trades a bounded leak for possible data loss, which inverts the crate's stated preference, and the safe fix is a seam change.

## The mechanism

`Drain::publish_prune` (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs`) publishes the shortened record, then journals what that dropped:

1. `publish_node(.., Some(applied.op_id))` — `publish_node` calls `mark_published(scope, op_id)` the moment `publish_head` acks. Its own doc states the ack, not the adopt, is where the op stops being replayable.
2. `owe_retires(scope, &plan.retire_targets)` — journals the dropped roots to the `RetireLedger`.

If step 2 fails with a seam error, `publish_prune` returns `Err`, but the shortened history is already live and the op is already marked published. Both continuations lose the debt:

- **Retry in the same pass.** `plan_prune` re-reads the now-shortened history, `plan.retire_targets` is empty, and the early return fires. Nothing is journaled.
- **Restart.** The published-op mark drops the op as already published, with the same result.

The dropped versions stay pinned and charged to the account with nothing naming them, and `pending_reclaim_bytes` never reports them. The ledger is the only record of the debt, and this path discards it silently.

## Why a replay cannot recover it

`crates/engine/src/seams/retire_ledger.rs` states the invariant that makes this terminal:

> once the shortened history publishes, nothing readable names the dropped roots, while a root always names its own leaves

So no later pass can reconstruct the doomed set from the record. Any failure after the publish is unrecoverable for that debt, not merely delayed.

## Why the obvious fix is wrong

The reviewer proposed journaling the owed entries before the publish. That is unsafe as the ledger stands. `drain_owed_retires` (`crates/engine/src/net/retire.rs`) retires every entry it reads with no check that the CID is unreachable, so an entry written before the publish can be acted on while a resolvable record still names the root. That unpins live content.

The crate ranks these outcomes explicitly, in `orphaned_head` in the same file:

> No ack is not proof nothing stored: unpinning a head a live record may still name is loss, where the row is only a leak.

The current ordering is therefore correct as written, and the doc comment on `publish_prune` states that rationale. The hole is the failure window it opens, not the order itself.

Retrying `owe_retires` in-pass — the reviewer's other suggestion — narrows the window but does not close it. A crash between the two steps, or a staging store that stays down, still loses the debt.

## What a real fix needs

An owed entry must be safe to hold while the old record is still live, so it can be journaled first. That means an unconfirmed state the drain skips, confirmed after the publish acks — a change to `OwedRetire`, to the `RetireLedger` trait, and to the conformance kit in `testkit::conformance::retire_ledger` that pins its contract.

An alternative worth weighing first: have `drain_owed_retires` establish unreachability itself before retiring, which would make a pre-publish entry harmless without a schema change, at the cost of a resolve per entry.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `RetireLedger::owe` failure after the record acks leaves the debt recoverable, and a later pass retires the dropped roots.
- The same holds across a process restart between the publish and the journal.
- No path retires a root that a resolvable record still names.
- `pending_reclaim_bytes` reports the debt for the whole window it is owed.
- A test drives the failure injection rather than asserting on source text.

## Scope note

The leak is bounded by what one prune drops and needs the staging store to fail in a narrow window, so this does not block the prune slice from landing.

every 60 s for 45–60 minutes and logged `settled= pending= failed=` on **every** iteration. Both
reported "CI DID NOT SETTLE" while CI had in fact been green for most of that time. A `cd` to the
repo as the first line of the background command did **not** hold. Rate limits were untouched
(5000/5000), which ruled out throttling and pointed straight at the cwd.

Reproduce: `(cd /tmp && env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh pr view 1145 --json mergeStateStatus)` fails.

**How to apply:** pass `--repo FSM1/cipher-box` on every `gh` call in any script, monitor, or
background task — it removes the cwd dependency entirely. `gh api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/...` is
already absolute and unaffected, which is why `recycle-both.sh`'s `gh api` polls kept working while
its sibling `gh pr view` calls went dark.

**Also treat an empty read as UNKNOWN, never as zero.** `pending=0` derived from a failed call looks
exactly like "nothing pending" and will score a red or unfinished PR as green — the same
false-all-clear shape as [[project-wave4-review-queue-state]]. Branch on `[ -z "$VAR" ]` first and
keep waiting.

When a CodeRabbit verdict comes back clean or nitpick-only and no further commit is needed, **leave
the PR in `ready`**. Do not re-draft it.

**Why:** the user stated it on 2026-08-08 — "this way a coderabbit slot is not mistakenly consumed on
a review that isn't necessary (when the pr is flipped to ready in the morning)". A draft→ready
transition starts a review, so re-drafting a clean PR means whoever merges it later pays a full
hourly slot for a review of a head that was already reviewed. With one review per hour org-wide
(see [[project-pr-reviewer-availability-aug-2026]]) that slot is the scarce resource.

**How to apply:**

- Clean or nitpick-only, no commit needed → leave READY.
- Actionable findings → re-draft **before** pushing the fix. A push onto a READY pr starts an
  incremental review and takes the slot the next pr in a chain is waiting for.
- Verdict never landed / unreadable → re-draft. That is the reversible side.
- To leave an already-drafted PR ready without burning a slot, flip it **after** another PR's flip
  has consumed the current hour. CodeRabbit answers with a rate-limit notice instead of a review and
  does not auto-retry, so the PR just sits ready.

Decide "clean" from the **inline comment count on the head**, not the review body text — a
nitpick-only review omits the `Actionable comments posted:` header entirely
([[project-coderabbit-verdict-two-surfaces]]).

Do not edit a cycle script while an instance of it is running; copy it and point the new run at the
copy. Editing a running bash script corrupted a run mid-flight on 2026-08-07.

**Refuted: the overwrite cannot happen.**

**A failed `owe_retires` loses the reclaim debt permanently.**

`publish_node` at Line 1711 passes `Some(applied.op_id)` as `completes`, so the published-op mark is raised the moment the record acks. If `owe_retires` at Line 1726 then fails with a seam error, `publish_prune` returns `Err(Halt::Unclassified)` and the op stays queued, but the shortened history is already live. Two outcomes follow:

- The pass retries the op. `plan_prune` now sees the shortened history, `plan.retire_targets` is empty, and Line 1674 returns `Ok(())`. The dropped roots are never journaled.
- The device restarts. The published-op mark drops the op as already published, with the same result.

The dropped versions then stay pinned and charged to the account forever, and `pending_reclaim_bytes` never reports them. This is a leak rather than data loss, which matches the crate's stated preference, but the ledger is the only record of the debt and this path silently discards it.

Consider journaling the owed entries before the publish and treating a pre-publish ledger entry as advisory, or retrying `owe_retires` within the pass before returning.

input.content:
---
name: project-gh-needs-repo-flag-in-background-shells
description: "Inline Bash-tool commands run under ZSH — a multi-word command or flag held in a variable does not word-split, so `$GH pr view` silently returns nothing"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

**The Bash tool's inline commands run under `zsh`, not bash.** zsh does **not** word-split unquoted
parameter expansions, so the bash idiom of stashing a multi-word command or flag in a variable breaks
silently:

```sh
GH="env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh"
$GH pr view 1146 --json statusCheckRollup     # zsh: command not found: env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh
R="--repo FSM1/cipher-box"
gh pr view 1146 $R --json ...                 # zsh: unknown flag: --repo FSM1/cipher-box
```

With `2>/dev/null` and `--jq`, both failures surface as an **empty string**, not an error — so a
poller reads "" and, if it treats empty as zero, scores a red or unfinished PR as green.

Cost on 2026-08-08: three CI watchers polled for 45–60 minutes each and logged `read FAILED` or
`settled= pending= failed=` on **every** iteration while CI had long been green. Diagnosed by running
the exact watcher line as a background probe: it printed `unknown flag` and `command not found`.

`recycle-both.sh` was immune all night because it is invoked as `bash script.sh` — inside a real bash
script the same idiom works. That contrast is the tell: if a snippet works in a `bash foo.sh` script
but returns nothing inline, suspect the shell, not the API.

**Wrong first diagnosis, recorded so it is not repeated:** the failure was initially blamed on
`gh` resolving the repo from the cwd, after a foreground `(cd /tmp && gh pr view ...)` failed with
`fatal: not a git repository`. That cwd failure is real but was a *different* failure reproduced by a
different command form, and `--repo` did not fix the watchers. Do not generalize a root cause from a
test whose command form differs from the failing one.

**How to apply in an inline Bash-tool command:**

- Write the command out in full — `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh pr view 1146 --repo FSM1/cipher-box ...`.
- Or put the loop in a `.sh` file and run it with `bash file.sh`.
- Never store a command prefix or a multi-word flag in a variable inline.
- Treat an empty read as **unknown** and keep waiting; never as zero. Branch on `[ -z "$VAR" ]`
  first — the same false-all-clear shape as [[project-wave4-review-queue-state]].

Separately, `gh pr view`/`gh pr checks` do resolve the repo from the cwd and fail outside a git repo;
`gh api repos/OWNER/NAME/...` is absolute and unaffected. Passing `--repo FSM1/cipher-box` is still
worth doing, just not the fix for this bug.

Related: [[feedback_gh_auth]] (always `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN`).

---
name: project-running-checkrun-conclusion-is-empty-string
description: "A RUNNING check-run has conclusion:\"\" not null, so `select(.conclusion==null)` counts zero pending and every CI gate built on it is a false all-clear"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

In `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup`, an in-flight **CheckRun** carries
`conclusion: ""` — an empty **string**. Only a pending **StatusContext** (CodeRabbit, Macroscope)
carries `conclusion: null`.

So the natural-looking jq is inverted:

```jq
select(.conclusion == null)   # pending  -> matches NO running check-run
select(.conclusion != null)   # settled  -> matches EVERY running check-run
```

`recycle-both.sh` used exactly this, and additionally *excluded* the reviewer StatusContexts from the
pending filter — so its `PEND` was **always 0** and the CI gate never gated on anything but the
`DONE >= MINCHECKS` count. That is why MINCHECKS mattered so much, and why raising it 15 → 30 changed
behaviour: the raw threshold was the only real gate. Fixed 2026-08-08.

**Correct form** (handles both null and `""`):

```jq
select((.conclusion // "") == "")   # pending
select((.conclusion // "") != "")   # settled
```

Proven live on PR #1171 while 4 checks were running: old logic reported `pending=0 settled=27`, new
logic `pending=4 settled=23`. The old form would have flipped the PR ready mid-run and consumed a
CodeRabbit slot on an unfinished build.

**Two related traps in the same rollup:**

- **`.name` vs `.context`** — CheckRun uses `.name`, StatusContext uses `.context`. Always
  `(.name // .context)`.
- **A review comment's `commit_id` is RE-ANCHORED to the current head** when its file and line still
  exist. So `select(.commit_id==$head)` reports an OLD finding as new — it briefly looked like a
  fresh CodeRabbit review had landed on #1158 when both comments predated the push by two hours. Use
  `.original_commit_id`, or fence on `.created_at` against a timestamp captured at flip time.

**How to apply:** any script deciding "is CI done" must use the `// ""` form, and must treat an empty
*read* (a failed API call) as unknown rather than zero — see
[[project-gh-needs-repo-flag-in-background-shells]]. Both failure modes point the same way: toward a
false all-clear, the recurring shape in [[project-wave4-review-queue-state]].

I found a defect in your `recycle-both.sh` while validating the new required context, and it is worth flagging before wave 8 starts.

**Its CI gate has never actually gated on running checks.** In `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup`, an in-flight check-run carries `conclusion: ""` — an empty *string*. Only a pending `StatusContext` (CodeRabbit, Macroscope) is `null`. The script tested `select(.conclusion==null)` for pending and then explicitly excluded those two reviewer contexts, so **`PEND` was always 0**. The only thing holding the flip back was `DONE >= MINCHECKS` — which is why MINCHECKS mattered so much, and why raising it from 15 to 30 changed behaviour.

Proven live on #1171 with four checks still running: the old filter reports `pending=0 settled=27`, the corrected one reports `pending=4 settled=23`. Under the old logic the script would have flipped it ready mid-build and spent a CodeRabbit slot on an unfinished run.

I fixed it in place — `(.conclusion // "") == ""` handles both the empty string and null — with a comment recording why, and applied the same fix to my own watcher. Nothing was running at the time. Every wave-7 flip is still sound: I confirmed each PR green by direct read before merging, and `mergeStateStatus=CLEAN` independently requires all required checks to have passed.

Related trap from last night, now also recorded: a review comment's `commit_id` is **re-anchored to the current head** when its file and line survive, so `commit_id==$head` reports old findings as new. That is what briefly made it look like #1158 had picked up a fresh review.

Wave 8 recon is still running; #1171 is re-watched with the corrected logic.

engine: prune must subtract retained versions before retiring a doomed root's leaves
---
## Problem

`expand_retire_targets` (`crates/engine/src/content/retention.rs`) expands **one** doomed version root into its leaf CIDs. It has no view of the versions the prune **retains**, so it cannot subtract a leaf that a retained version also references.

The registry's pin row is keyed `(account, cid)` — per account and CID, not per version (`blueprint/api.md` "Pin/name registry") — and physical unpin fires at global refcount zero. So if a doomed version's root manifest names a CID a retained version also names, retiring the doomed version deletes the account's single row for that CID and unpins live content.

## Why it is not reachable today, and why that changes

For honestly-authored versions the leaf sets are disjoint by construction: `ContentKey::generate` mints a fresh per-version content key and `seal_one_chunk` draws a fresh random 24-byte nonce per chunk (`crates/engine/src/content/chunk.rs`), so identical plaintext seals to different CIDs in different versions. There is no copy or dedup op that makes two live records share a `contentCid`.

The reachable path is adversarial and crosses a privilege boundary. Per `blueprint/api.md`, a write-grantee's uploads register under the grantee's account until the owner's client syncs and registers them too. A malicious write-grantee in a shared scope can author a version whose root block's `links` array names the owner's live leaf CIDs. That block content-addresses correctly, and `decode_root`'s `links.len() == ceil(size/chunkSize)` check is satisfiable by choosing `size`, so the expansion accepts it. The owner's routine prune then retires the owner's own live leaves.

The `PinnedBytesMismatch` gate added alongside the expansion does not close this: the grantee controls the `Version.size` the plan derives `pinned_bytes` from, so they control both sides of that equality.

## Why it belongs with the prune op, not the expansion

The retained set is a whole-plan property. `expand_retire_targets` sees one root; only the caller that decided which versions are doomed and which are retained knows the union of the retained expansions. Passing a `retained: &BTreeSet<String>` into the expansion ahead of that caller would be speculative — and it breaks the closed-form pinned-bytes accounting, since a subtracted leaf frees zero bytes and the total is no longer `size + 40n + root_len`.

## Fix

When the prune op is wired, subtract the union of the retained versions' expansions from each doomed version's targets before retiring, and sum the reclaim figure over the surviving targets rather than over the whole manifest.

Acceptance:

- A doomed root naming a retained version's leaf does not retire that leaf.
- The reclaim figure for an aliased expansion counts only the bytes it actually frees.

## Gate

`Engine Tests`.

ci: install wasm-bindgen-cli from a prebuilt binary - blocked on the Actions allowlist
---
## What

`.github/actions/wasm-bindgen-cli` builds `wasm-bindgen-cli` from source with `cargo install`. Measured on a cache-cold run: **104s**, in every job that touches wasm — `Web Engine WASM`, `Core KATs`, `Client Browser Suite`, the `web-e2e.yml` fallback, and `deploy-staging.yml`'s `Build Web App`.

Since the wasm engine is now built once per run by a producer job that its consumers wait on, that 104s sits on the critical path. It is the single reason the build-once split trades wall-clock for runner minutes instead of winning both: the producer job is 158s, of which 104s is acquiring the CLI and 31s is the actual build.

`~/.cargo/bin` is cached, so the install is skipped on a warm cache — but cache entries are scoped to the writing ref, so a PR's first run is always cold.

## Blocked on an Actions-allowlist decision

The clean fix is a prebuilt binary. Attempted and reverted: `taiki-e/install-action` (upstream's checksum-verified release archive, `wasm-bindgen` is in its manifest for Linux/macOS/Windows). It fails at the runner:

```text
The action taiki-e/install-action@<sha> is not allowed in FSM1/cipher-box because
all actions must be from a repository owned by FSM1, created by GitHub, verified
in the GitHub Marketplace, or match one of the patterns: GabrielBB/xvfb-action*,
appleboy/*, bytecodealliance/actions*, docker/*, dorny/paths-filter*,
gabrielbb/xvfb-action*, ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres*, pnpm/*, tauri-apps/*
```

Two ways forward, and the choice is a policy call, not a code one:

1. **Add `taiki-e/*` to the repository's allowed-actions patterns**, then pin `taiki-e/install-action` by SHA in the composite. Keeps checksum verification and cross-platform support; costs one more third-party action in the supply chain.
2. **Fetch the upstream release tarball with `curl` inside the composite.** Needs no allowlist change, but hardcodes a platform triple into an action used by five jobs and gives up the checksum verification unless a `sha256` is pinned alongside the version — which then has to be updated in lockstep with every `wasm-bindgen` bump, reintroducing exactly the two-places-to-edit drift the composite removed.

Option 1 is preferred. Whichever lands must keep the current invariant: the CLI version derives from `Cargo.lock`, and an unreadable lockfile aborts rather than resolving a floating version.

## Gate

- A cache-cold run of `Web Engine WASM` spends under 15s acquiring `wasm-bindgen-cli`.
- The version still derives from `Cargo.lock`, and a deliberate mismatch still fails the run.
- `Core KATs` still gets `wasm-bindgen-test-runner` from the same install.
- `deploy-staging.yml`'s `Build Web App` no longer pays a from-source install.

web: decide the Core Kit storage scope and gate its key set
---
## Goal

Decide, and write down, what the Web3Auth Core Kit store is allowed to persist and where.

## Problem

`apps/web/src/auth/coreKit.ts` passes `storage: window.localStorage` to `Web3AuthMPCCoreKit`, inherited from v1. Core Kit writes two things into it:

- `setDeviceFactor` persists a raw `factorKey` hex — a tKey share scalar — once MFA is enabled.
- `createSession` persists a `sessionId`, the handle for a session payload holding `postBoxKey`, `factorKey`, `tssShare`, and `signatures`. Anyone who reads that id can reconstitute a logged-in Core Kit and call `_UNSAFE_exportTssKey`.

Default `sessionTime` is 86400s, and `localStorage` survives tab close and is shared across every tab on the origin. So any same-origin XSS or shared-machine reader gets a 24-hour bearer path to the login secret.

The login secret itself is never written — it leaves the UI realm only as the transferred buffer — so this is not a violation of AGENTS.md rule 1 on its face. But the store is a credential, it is currently a default rather than a decision, and #911 shipped with only a code comment naming the tension.

## Work

Pick and justify:

- `sessionStorage` — per-tab, cleared on close. Still survives reload, which is all the `useAuth` restore effect needs. Costs cross-tab session restore, which the one-leader tab model may already make moot.
- An explicit, shorter `sessionTime`.
- Keeping `localStorage` deliberately, with the reasoning recorded.

Then make the accepted storage key set an assertion in the web-e2e login spec, so a future SDK bump that starts persisting something new fails a gate instead of a review. The current unit test cannot see this: it runs against a fake session with no SDK behind it.

## Gate

web-e2e login spec. `tests/web-e2e/` now exists (#809, #1078) and carries a login spec, so the assertion has somewhere to land — note that CI logs in through the introspection hook rather than an interactive Core Kit session, so the spec needs to reach a real Core Kit path or assert the absence of unexpected keys under the hook path deliberately.

## Dependencies

None outstanding. #804 (the `coreKit.ts` storage choice) and #809 (the web-e2e harness the gate runs in) have both landed.

engine: the register and retire CID-set derivations are unlinked
---
## Problem

The set of CIDs one version pins is now derived in two places that nothing binds together.

**Produce side** — `registry_cids` (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs`) emits the root first, then every leaf in file order. Its own doc states the contract: "Registration and retirement both go through here, so a retire batch names exactly what a register batch claimed — and every block is its own accountable pin row, so leaving a leaf out of a retirement spends account quota forever." It is live, reached from `registered_by` for op-abandonment retires, and it recovers the leaf CIDs from **staging**.

**Consume side** — `expand_retire_targets` (`crates/engine/src/content/retention.rs`) emits every leaf, then the root last, and recovers the leaf CIDs from the **fetched root block**.

The two orderings differ for a real reason: the expansion key differs. The op-drain path reads its leaves from staging, so the root is not load-bearing and root-first is harmless. The prune path fetches the root block long after staging released the leaves, so the root **is** the expansion key and must outlive what it expands to. Both are correct for their own path.

What is missing is anything holding the two **sets** equal. As sets they agree today — both run every CID through `encode_content_cid_str`, and retire is set-semantic and idempotent — but no shared function and no test asserts it. Drift is silent and consequential in both directions: under-naming leaves blocks pinned and charged forever (the defect the expansion exists to fix), over-naming unpins live blocks.

`registry_cids`'s doc claim that retirement goes through it also stops being true once the prune drain is wired.

## Fix

When the prune drain lands, unify the two into one CID-set derivation with the retire ordering as an explicit parameter of the call rather than a property of which function you happened to reach, and pin it:

```rust
#[test]
fn the_retire_expansion_names_exactly_what_registration_pinned() {
    // sorted(registry_cids(root, leaves)) == sorted(expand_retire_targets(version, block))
}
```

Correct `registry_cids`'s doc at the same time so it describes the paths that actually reach it.

Deliberately not done in the PR that introduced the expansion: `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs` was owned by a parallel branch in that wave, and the unification wants the prune drain in place to know which ordering each call site needs.

## Gate

`Engine Tests`.

# Wave 8 shared brief — read this fully before you touch anything

Repo: `FSM1/cipher-box`. Main checkout `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box` at `a4683d0a3`.
**Never touch the main checkout.** Work only in the worktree your task names.

## Shell traps that have already cost this project hours

- Inline shell commands here run under **zsh**, which does NOT word-split unquoted variables. Never
  write `GH="env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh"` then `$GH pr view` — it fails with `command not found` and,
  with `2>/dev/null`, returns an EMPTY string that reads as a valid answer. Write commands out in
  full, or put the loop in a `.sh` file and run `bash file.sh`.
- Every `gh` call needs `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN` (a stale `GITHUB_TOKEN` causes 401s) and, for
  `gh pr`/`gh issue`, `--repo FSM1/cipher-box`.
- In `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup`, a RUNNING check has `conclusion: ""` — an empty string,
  not null. `select(.conclusion==null)` matches nothing. Use `(.conclusion // "") == ""` for pending.
- `git worktree add` forks the LOCAL branch ref, which may be stale. Always
  `git reset --hard origin/<branch>` right after creating a worktree.

## Build hygiene

- Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in your worktree. Do NOT symlink `node_modules`.
- Do NOT set or share `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. Each worktree uses its own `target/`, or you get stale
  test binaries that pass while the source is broken.
- Rebuild dependent `dist` before a cross-package typecheck (`pnpm build`).
- `apps/web` vitest collects `*.test.ts(x)` ONLY. A `.spec.ts` file is silently skipped.

## Gates — all must pass before you push

Rust:

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
cargo check -p cipherbox-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
```

`cargo fmt` must be `--all`. Never scope it with `-p` — the CI gate is `--all` and a scoped run
leaves other crates unformatted. Note `--workspace` never builds `wasm32`, which is why the last
command is separate.

TypeScript:

```
pnpm typecheck
pnpm lint
pnpm lint:tracker-refs
pnpm test
```

## Code law (AGENTS.md — CI or review will reject a breach)

1. All crypto lives in `crates/core`. TypeScript never implements crypto or a codec.
2. Determinism is injected. Never call a clock or an RNG directly in core/engine logic — entropy,
   time and policy arrive as parameters or seam traits.
3. **Encode/decode fail-closed symmetry.** If a decode path hard-rejects an invariant, the matching
   encode path MUST enforce it with a **release-active** check returning `Err` — never
   `debug_assert!`, which is stripped in release. Follow `crates/core/src/seal/body.rs`
   `assert_children_unique`, and cover it with a test that fires in a release build.
4. Zeroize at the **terminal owner only**. A callee must never zero a buffer its caller still owns.
5. Prefer TypeScript string literals over `enum`.
6. Use the `CONTEXT.md` ubiquitous language exactly. `publicKey`/`privateKey`/`ipnsName` in full
   camelCase for API fields, snake_case for database columns.

## Comment law

Comments explain **why**, never what, and stay short. All three of these are rejected on sight:

- **Absence-justifying comments** — prose explaining why a path that is not in the code cannot
  happen. It rots into a falsehood the moment that path is wired.
- **Unchanged-code apologia** — a doc block defending code your diff does not modify.
- **Tracker references** — a bare `#1234` in code. `pnpm lint:tracker-refs` is a CI gate. State the
  checkable condition instead: "the real wiring is not landed", not "see #1026". Citations of the
  frozen decision corpus (`FSM1/cipher-box-next#32`, or a bare one/two-digit `#NN`) are exempt.

State a rationale ONCE, at its home (the type or definition), not on every caller.

## Tests

- Assert runtime behaviour, never source text. A grep-shaped assertion has previously forced a
  runtime-broken implementation that only an e2e caught.
- Prove each new test actually fails without your change. Temporarily revert the production code,
  watch it go red, restore it, and report that you did this. This is not optional.

## Git and PR rules

- Branch from `main`. Never push to `main`.
- Branch names: `feat/`, `fix/`, `docs/`, `refactor/`, `chore/`, `test/`, `ci/`, `perf/`.
- Conventional Commits. **No parentheses anywhere in the subject line** — it breaks Release Please.
  CI validates the PR title.
- End every commit message with:
  `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`
- Open the PR as a **DRAFT**. Never run `gh pr ready` — the orchestrator controls review timing
  because CodeRabbit allows one review per hour across the whole org.
- **Never write a closing keyword you intend to negate.** "Does not close #1016" STILL auto-closes
  #1016. If you must mention an issue you are not closing, write it without the keyword.
- Use `Closes #N` only for an issue this PR fully finishes. Use `Part of #N` only for umbrellas.
- No Claude attribution in the PR body.
- Escape a `#NN` in the PR body only when it is NOT an issue reference.

## Review gates you must run yourself on your own diff (`git diff main...HEAD`)

1. `/simplify` — remove speculative generality, dead abstraction, duplication.
2. `/security-review` — trust boundaries, fail-closed behaviour, auth/expiry gates, injection,
   resource exhaustion, concurrency, determinism seams.
3. `/crypto-privacy-review` — **required if your diff touches crypto**: `crates/core` primitives,
   key or seal material, or a trust-boundary read.

If a slash command is unavailable, do a rigorous manual pass against that checklist instead. Never
skip a gate. Fold real findings back into the code and tests before you report done.

## Reporting

Report: what you changed and why, the exact gate exit codes, new test names, your red-proof for
each new test, the pushed commit sha, and the PR number. If a task turns out to be wrong, already
done, or a bad idea, say so plainly with file:line evidence instead of inventing a change.

My merge check does not work in this repo: PRs are squash-merged, so branch ancestry is never preserved and `--is-ancestor` reports every branch as unmerged regardless. I deleted nothing rather than act on a check I now know is wrong for this merge strategy. **#1139 is out of the parallel set and queued behind P3.** P4 wrote no code and left its branch untouched, which is what I wanted over a forced fix.

Its finding is recorded on #1139, and one part changes the deliverable:

**The write history link recovers the *previous* seed, not the fresh one.** A link sealed under the new epoch's key yields the prior seed from the new root — which is exactly what `blueprint/engine.md:419` needs so a resumed name wave can enumerate and retire old interior names. But the fresh seed stays reachable only via pointer → new root → owner-write blob, so a crash between root republish and pointer flip leaves it genuinely unreachable, and "mint a new one" remains correct there. The issue title reads wider than the fix delivers, and whoever wires `resume_write_scope_seed` must not be told otherwise.

It also flagged that a resume test written against the in-memory fake would be worthless — `mid_wave_crash_resumes_from_published_records_only` already passes by handing the seed back in memory. The resume only means anything across the publisher/resolver seam.

And a tracker-shaped gap: `rotate_scope_write` has **no production caller** — it is reached only from tests. That is the "faked seam" pattern that hides work from the tracker, so it is worth checking whether an issue covers it.

## #913 — the decision, and why it went the other way

**Decision: keep `localStorage`, and bound the window with an explicit `sessionTime` instead of the storage scope.** The defined default (`sessionStorage`) would have broken a real flow.

**Evidence.** Cross-tab Core Kit restore *is* load-bearing — the one-leader model does not make it moot, it makes it mandatory:

- `packages/client/src/engineClient.ts:322-375` — `promote()` calls `provideFailoverSecret()` → `SecretSource.provideSecret()`, which throws outright with no source.
- `apps/web/src/engine/loginHandoff.ts:63-77` — `LoginSecretSource.provideSecret` calls `_UNSAFE_exportTssKey()` on **this tab's** Core Kit. The secret never crosses the BroadcastChannel; `packages/client/src/broadcastTransport.ts:143-152` says a follower never receives it.
- `apps/web/src/auth/CoreKitProvider.tsx:45-49` builds a session and calls `restore()` **per tab**; `apps/web/src/auth/useAuth.ts:151-157` arms the secret source only after that tab's own handoff, gated on `session.isLoggedIn()`.

So under `sessionStorage`, a tab the user did not personally log in through (bookmark, second window) renders signed out *and*, when the leader dies, aborts promotion — the origin loses its engine and every remaining tab churns the lock.

**Cost accepted:** the store stays readable by any same-origin script. Both review passes independently established the value in it is not an opaque handle — `corekit_store.sessionId` is a secp256k1 scalar that both addresses and decrypts a Web3Auth-held record carrying `postBoxKey`/`factorKey`/`signatures`, with no `allowedOrigin` binding. The comment now says that rather than the reassuring half.

**`sessionTime` = 8h, not 2h.** I started at 2h; both reviews found in the SDK source that `sessionTime` also feeds `Torus.setSessionTime` → `session_token_exp_second`, which expires the `signatures` `_UNSAFE_exportTssKey` needs. 2h would have capped the *working session* at 2h and made a mid-session failover promotion fail silently over a UI still rendering signed in. 8h outlasts a working day and still does not survive a night on a shared machine (24h does).

**Also fixed, found by the crypto pass:** the SDK's `logout()` blanks its session id *in place* and leaves the rest of its store standing — a device factor share included, once MFA is reachable. `Web3AuthSession.logout()` now clears the store, on the refused path too.

## #914 — BLOCKED, not attempted

Threading a session/auth event unavoidably edits `crates/engine/src/facade.rs`, which you told me to stop on:

- The `Event` enum is `facade.rs:598-660`; Rust cannot extend it from another file.
- `Command::Logout` (`facade.rs:521`) has **no arm at all** — it falls through to `Unimplemented` at `facade.rs:2373`. `Engine::start` (`facade.rs:1672-1818`) emits nothing auth-shaped. Both emit sites are in `facade.rs`.
- No facade getter for session state exists (`Engine.started` is private, `Engine::session()` is `pub(crate)`).

Downstream is then mechanical: `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs:736-747` (exhaustive `kind` match, compiler-enforced) + a payload getter; `packages/client/src/worker/protocol.ts:163` union; `commandCodec.ts:255` `readEvent` (its `default` throws). Items 2–4 all hang off item 1 — item 4's guard is specified "on top of the derived state" — so I landed none of it rather than half-land a guard the next batch rewrites. Sequence me and it is a small diff.

## Gates (all in the worktree, exit codes)

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` = 0 (diff contains no Rust; clippy/test/wasm-check skipped for that reason). `pnpm typecheck` = 0, `pnpm lint` = 0, `pnpm lint:tracker-refs` = 0, `pnpm test` = 0 (261 web / 401 client / 179 api). Full `web-e2e` run against a live local stack: **6 passed**.

## New tests and red-proofs (every one proven red)

`apps/web/src/auth/coreKit.test.ts`:
- *persists origin-wide…* — red via `storage: window.sessionStorage` → `AssertionError: expected Storage{…(1)} to be Storage{…(3)}`.
- *caps how long a persisted session stays restorable…* — red via `sessionTime: 86_400` → `expected 86400 to be less than 86400`. Keeps `toBeGreaterThan(0)` deliberately: the SDK restores 86400s on a **falsy** value, so an upper bound alone passes on `0`.

`tests/web-e2e/tests/smoke.spec.ts` *the login flow leaves nothing outside the storage allow-list* — red by adding one `localStorage.setItem` to `main.tsx` and rebuilding the bundle.

## Two things you should know

1. **I edited `tests/web-e2e/tests/smoke.spec.ts`, not a `login*` file.** `tests/web-e2e/playwright.config.ts` sets `testMatch: '**/smoke.spec.ts'` for the `e2e` project — a new `login.spec.ts` would never run, and P1 owns that config. Appended at end of file to minimise conflict.

content.text:
**P7 landed #913 and reversed my call on the strength of the evidence — the right outcome.**

**The decision went to `localStorage` with a bounded `sessionTime`, not `sessionStorage`.** My hypothesis was that the one-leader tab model made cross-tab restore moot. It is the opposite: cross-tab restore is *mandatory*. A follower holds no keys and never receives the login secret, so when the leader dies, promotion re-exports it from **that tab's own** Core Kit. Under `sessionStorage`, a tab the user did not personally log in through has no exporter, `provideSecret()` rejects, and the origin loses its engine while every remaining tab churns the lock. I verified all three claims against the branch.

Two things it found that neither of us anticipated:

- **`sessionTime` is not just a storage lifetime.** It also feeds `Torus.setSessionTime` → `session_token_exp_second`, which expires the `signatures` that `_UNSAFE_exportTssKey` needs. The 2h it first chose would have capped the *working session* at 2h and made a mid-session failover fail silently over a UI still rendering signed in. It settled on 8h — outlasts a working day, does not survive a night on a shared machine.
- **A real bug in logout.** The SDK's `logout()` blanks the session id in place and leaves the rest of the store standing, including a device factor share once MFA is reachable. Now cleared, including on the refused path.

**#914 is blocked and correctly not attempted.** Threading a session/auth event needs `crates/engine/src/facade.rs` — the `Event` enum lives there, `Command::Logout` has no arm at all and falls through to `Unimplemented`, and there is no facade getter for session state. Items 2–4 all hang off item 1, so it landed none rather than half-landing a route guard the next batch would rewrite. **That makes the wave 8 PRs, not 7** — a discovery, not scope creep, and #914 has to follow P5 which owns `facade.rs`.

**Two things I had to correct after it:**

- **#1175 was filed orphaned** — no parent, no component label, no milestone. Now under #642 with `comp:web` and the milestone, matching #913's parentage.
- **A conflict I am now watching:** P7 edited `tests/web-e2e/tests/smoke.spec.ts`, which P1 owns. It had a good reason — `testMatch: '**/smoke.spec.ts'` means a new `login.spec.ts` would never run — and it appended at end of file to minimise overlap, but P1 is actively changing that same file to fix the flake. I will check the pairwise merge before the second of them lands.

#1174 is draft and `CLEAN`. Still running: P1, P2, P3.

**The web-e2e flake investigation refuted its own best story, which is the useful part.**

The tempting conclusion was that the flake began on 2026-08-05. It did not. **The `Web E2E Smoke` job did not exist before then** — it was created by `3d087d673` when #1078 merged. So there are zero prior executions and no before/after to compare. "Failures started 08-05" is entirely explained by "the job started existing on 08-05". The first failure is the 12th execution ever, about two hours after the gate merged. **The gate never had a clean period**; it started observing a condition already present in `main`.

The real numbers: 126 executions, 116 that ran, 8 failures — of which **two are infra, not Playwright** (a TS build error on `FetchEventLike.waitUntil`, and a missing `web-engine-wasm` artifact). That gives **6 genuine flakes in 114 runs, 5.3%**. I have told P1 to use those figures and count the infra pair separately.

**One methodological finding I have added to memory, because it is the same failure class that bit me twice today.** The agent's first census used `2>/dev/null` with no retry. Transient GitHub connection refusals silently dropped **13 of 126 rows — including the very first failure it was hunting**. It only caught this because a spot check surfaced a job the census claimed did not exist. A dropped row is indistinguishable from a clean result. Any `gh` sweep needs retries and an explicit count of unrecoverable reads.

---
## Problem

`WriteWaveNet::reseal_root` carries `plane.write_body.write_history_link` verbatim into the moved root's re-sealed write body (`crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs`, the `CommittedSet` it hands `reseal_scope_root`).

`WriteBody` is sealed under `writeScopeSeed`, which **every** write grantee holds — including the one the rotation is cutting. `write_history_link` is opaque bytes (`crates/core/src/seal/write_body.rs`), no owner signature covers it, `enforce_committed_ledger` does not reach it, and `reseal_scope_root` copies it unexamined.

## Why it matters

Two compounding problems:

1. **Semantic wrong-seed.** The wave mints a *fresh* `writeScopeSeed` but republishes the *pre-rotation* write history link, so the moved root's link does not chain to the seed it was just re-keyed to.
2. **Capability widening once seed recovery lands.** `RotateScopeWritePlan::resume_write_scope_seed` is documented as "the fresh write scope seed recovered from the published root (the write-plane history link)" (`crates/engine/src/rotation/rotate_write.rs`), and that recovery wiring is not landed. When it lands, a revoked write grantee who plants a forged `writeHistoryLink` before the wave gets the **owner to sign it into the new root**, and the resumed wave then republishes the whole subtree under names derived from an attacker-chosen seed. Total write-plane takeover, in a record that is owner-authentic — no gate stage can catch it.

The only thing keeping this latent is that the recovery is unbuilt.

## Resolving

The wave must mint its own link rather than carry one: either pass an empty `write_history_link` from `reseal_root` (the wave holds its own seed; recovery is not this record's job), or extend `ResealSeeds` with a write-plane `prev` and have `reseal_scope_root` seal a fresh link over the retiring `writeScopeSeed` under `write_key(fresh_seed)`, mirroring the read-plane `prev` path.

Independently, when the seed recovery lands it must cross-check `derive_write_name(recovered_seed, scope_id) == published root name` before a single republish — the reverse of the check `publish_moved` already makes in the forward direction.

## Gate

Engine unit:

- a planted `writeHistoryLink` on the pre-wave root is never re-signed into the moved root
- a resumed wave refuses a recovered write scope seed that does not derive the published root name

## Notes

Found by the `/security-review` gate on #1177. Pre-existing; the fix lands in `crates/engine/src/rotation/reseal.rs` and `rotate_write.rs`, owned by other slices.

## What changed — PR #1173 (draft), branch `fix/prune-retention-aliasing`, head `3969b37da`

### #1124 — prune subtracts the retained versions

`Drain::prune_debt` (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs`) expands every doomed **and** every retained version off its own fetched root block — **ahead of the publish**, so a debt the pass cannot compute leaves the history it read standing — and subtracts the union of the retained expansions from each doomed target set. `OwedRetire` (`crates/engine/src/seams/retire_ledger.rs`) gained `retained` (the aliased CIDs, normally empty) and `manifest_bytes` (the expansion's bound), so `retire_owed` skips them and `owed_bytes` is what the retire actually frees. `Expansion` now carries a per-target byte figure (`RetireTarget`) because a subtracted leaf frees nothing and the closed form `size + 40n + root_len` no longer holds.

### #1125 — one CID-set derivation

`registry_cids` is gone. Both paths go through `version_cids(root, leaves, RootPlacement)` in `content/retention.rs`, with the ordering an explicit argument **of the call**. `the_retire_expansion_names_exactly_what_registration_pinned` pins the two sets equal.

## #1152 — wasm-bindgen-cli from a prebuilt binary

`taiki-e/install-action@6c6fd71fe4fb72c3697d269963d0e15df8adedad # v2.85.10`, SHA-pinned (SHA verified against the tag). **Measured on this PR's own runs: the whole composite takes 11–16s** vs 104s for the install alone. All five call sites pass. `~/.cargo/bin` dropped from four cache path lists — it held only the from-source build.

Three hardening changes came from the security pass, not from me:
- The Cargo.lock version becomes an install-action tool spec, and **that input splits on whitespace and commas** — `version = "0.2.126 evil-crate"` survived the old `sed` and would have `cargo install`ed a second unpinned crate. Now requires a bare three-part version. The old `cargo install ... --version "$V"` was injection-proof by construction; the rewrite lost that, and I put it back.
- **`fallback: none`**, not `cargo-install`. The default `cargo-binstall` wants `github.token`, and on a version the pinned manifest lacks it silently trades the archive's sha256 for an unverified source build — the exact cost this change removes, and it would go green.
- A step asserts the CLI on PATH is the locked version; install-action prints it but asserts nothing.

## #1169 — the flake

**The issue's premise is wrong and I did not implement what it asked for.** It is not a first-paint race: `goto` completes cleanly and the next call dies ~1s later. The `toBeVisible` failure *aborted* at 1321ms against a 5000ms budget, and one failure died inside a `waitForFunction` — itself a readiness wait. No timeout or readiness condition could fix either.

Root cause, from `DEBUG=pw:browser` on a probe run: **`Received signal 11 SEGV_MAPERR`**. Playwright's default `chrome-headless-shell` segfaults on a page that registers a Service Worker. Fix is `channel: 'chromium'` — Chrome's own headless.

I could not reproduce locally (16 runs, then 200 executions at 2 workers with the box CPU-saturated, all green), so I A/B'd in CI on throwaway branches at `--repeat-each=25`, 125 executions per run:

| probe | runs failed |
|---|---|
| unchanged | 2 of 3 |
| after the `NODE_ENV` fix, still on the shell | 2 of 3 |
| `serviceWorkers: 'block'` | 0 of 3 |
| `channel: 'chromium'` | 0 of 3 |
| **final, merged content** | **0 of 3** |

Blocking Service Workers also works but drops production behaviour from a gate whose premise is that the shipping artifact is the one tested.

Two further defects surfaced on the way, both fixed:
- **The suite was testing development bundles.** `NODE_ENV: test` sat at job scope, and Vite reads it to decide whether a build is production. `release-bundle.spec.ts` — whose entire subject is the shipping artifact — was asserting against a dev build. Two new tests assert the tab comes under `/sw.js`; red-proved in one run against both bundles side by side (`[release]` passed, `[e2e]` built with `NODE_ENV=test` failed with `Received has value: null`).
- **The per-test login secret was published** as a `page.evaluate` argument, recorded verbatim into a trace this public repo uploads. Now minted in-page.

`tests/web-e2e/fixtures.ts` taps console/pageerror/requestfailed/crash/close and fails with the cause — it is what surfaced the MIME error that unravelled this.

Both changes landed as described. **Cumulative gates pass on all four merged at `b393d97ed`** — 1661 Rust tests, 841 TS.

**P1 (#1172) found that #1169's premise was wrong and said so instead of implementing it.** The flake is not a first-paint race. `goto` completes cleanly; the `toBeVisible` failure *aborted* at 1321 ms against a 5000 ms budget, and one failure died inside a `waitForFunction` — itself a readiness wait. No timeout or readiness condition could have fixed either.

The actual cause, from `DEBUG=pw:browser`: **`Received signal 11 SEGV_MAPERR`. Playwright's default `chrome-headless-shell` segfaults on a page that registers a Service Worker.** The fix is one line — `channel: 'chromium'`.

It could not reproduce locally across 200 executions, so it **A/B'd in CI on throwaway branches at `--repeat-each=25`**, 125 executions per run:

| probe | runs failed |
|---|---|
| unchanged | 2 of 3 |
| `NODE_ENV` fix only | 2 of 3 |
| `serviceWorkers: 'block'` | 0 of 3 |
| `channel: 'chromium'` | 0 of 3 |

That design is why the answer is trustworthy: the third row confirms the service-worker trigger the earlier agent suspected, while the fourth shows the real defect was the browser binary, not our code.

**Two further defects it surfaced on the way:**

- **The suite was testing development bundles.** `NODE_ENV: test` sat at job scope and Vite reads it to decide production-ness — so `release-bundle.spec.ts`, whose entire subject is the shipping artifact, was asserting against a dev build.
- **The per-test login secret was passed as a `page.evaluate` argument**, recorded verbatim into traces this **public** repo uploads.

On that last one, the bounded read: the secret is minted fresh per test via `randomBytes(32)` and the API creates the account on first login, so each exposure is a throwaway account, **not** the shared `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET`. **No credential rotation is needed.** It is now generated in-page so it never crosses the evaluate boundary.

Its own security pass also caught an injection it had introduced: the `Cargo.lock` version becomes an install-action tool spec, and that input splits on whitespace — `version = "0.2.126 evil-crate"` would have installed a second unpinned crate. The old `cargo install --version` form was injection-proof by construction; the rewrite lost that, and it put it back. It also set `fallback: none`, since the default silently trades a verified archive for an unverified source build **and still goes green**.

It corrected two of its own earlier claims and rewrote branch history so no commit carries them.

**All four PRs are draft and CLEAN: #1172, #1173, #1174, #1177.** Ready for review cycles whenever you want them started — merge order P1 → P7 → P2 → P3, with P7 rebased after P1 so its CI exercises the `smoke.spec.ts` combination.

#!/bin/bash
# Wave 8 review chain, in merge order. One CodeRabbit slot per pr, and the hourly
# slot runs from when a review STARTS, so each pr's earliest flip is derived from
# the PREVIOUS flip rather than the previous verdict.
#   $1 = epoch the first pr may flip at (default: now)
set -u
RECYCLE=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-myankelev-Code-random-cipher-box/2b9a962d-e9c8-4465-b4ef-93584f21a390/scratchpad/recycle-keepready.sh
LOGDIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-myankelev-Code-random-cipher-box/2b9a962d-e9c8-4465-b4ef-93584f21a390/scratchpad
PREV_FLIP=${1:-$(date -u +%s)}
FIRST=1

# recycle prints the flip as a bare HH:MM:SSZ, so the date has to be put back on
# it. A reconstruction landing in the future belongs to yesterday.
flip_epoch_from_log() {
  local t now e
  t=$(grep -m1 -oE "FLIPPED READY [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z" "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $3}')
  now=$(date -u +%s)
  if [ -z "$t" ]; then echo "$now"; return; fi
  e=$(date -u -j -f "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ" "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)T${t}" +%s 2>/dev/null || echo "$now")
  [ "$e" -gt "$now" ] && e=$((e - 86400))
  echo "$e"
}

for PR in 1172 1174 1173 1177; do
  if [ "$FIRST" = "1" ]; then NB=$PREV_FLIP; FIRST=0; else NB=$((PREV_FLIP + 3660)); fi
  LOG=""
  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    LOG="$LOGDIR/w8-cycle-$PR-$attempt.log"
    echo "=== #$PR attempt $attempt, notbefore=$(date -u -r "$NB" +%H:%M:%SZ) ==="
    MINCHECKS=25 bash "$RECYCLE" "$PR" "$NB" >"$LOG" 2>&1
    echo "#$PR rc=$? (log $LOG)"
    grep -E "CI GREEN|CI FAILED|FLIPPED|CR VERDICT|MACROSCOPE|RE-DRAFTED|LEFT READY|actionable|WARNING|INCOMPLETE|CANNOT|COULD NOT" "$LOG" | sed 's/^/   /'

    # A flip inside the cooldown is answered with a rate-limit notice instead of a
    # review, and consumes no slot - so retry rather than lose the pr's verdict.
    LIMU=$(env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments \
      --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("Review limit reached";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // ""' 2>/dev/null)
    LIMEP=0
    [ -n "$LIMU" ] && LIMEP=$(date -u -j -f "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ" "$LIMU" +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    if [ "$LIMEP" -gt "$NB" ] 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "#$PR RATE LIMITED at $LIMU - retrying in 21m"
      NB=$(( $(date -u +%s) + 1260 ))
      continue
    fi
    break
  done
  PREV_FLIP=$(flip_epoch_from_log "$LOG")
  echo "#$PR flip epoch=$PREV_FLIP ($(date -u -r "$PREV_FLIP" +%H:%M:%SZ)); next slot $(date -u -r $((PREV_FLIP+3660)) +%H:%M:%SZ)"
done

echo "=== WAVE 8 REVIEW CHAIN COMPLETE $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ) ==="
for PR in 1172 1174 1173 1177; do
  echo "#$PR isDraft=$(env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh pr view $PR --repo FSM1/cipher-box --json isDraft --jq '.isDraft' 2>/dev/null)"
done

Anchoring the namespace instead (`loglevel(?::[\w.-]+)?`) closes the `loglevel-anything` hole without breaking the suite. #1175 web: seal the Core Kit store under a non-extractable key [OPEN] labels=v2-build,comp:web

## Goal

Stop the Core Kit store from holding a script-readable bearer capability.

## Problem

#913 decided the store stays origin-wide, because `EngineClient.promote` re-exports the login
secret from the promoted tab's own restored Core Kit session and has no other source. That
decision is right, but it leaves what the store holds unchanged: `corekit_store.sessionId` is a
secp256k1 scalar that both addresses and decrypts a Web3Auth-held record carrying `postBoxKey`,
`factorKey`, `tssShare` and `signatures`. The session manager is constructed with no
`allowedOrigin`, so possession alone redeems it — from any origin, on any machine.

Any script that reaches the origin reads 32 bytes and replays them offline for the whole
`sessionTime` window. What it gets back exports the login secret, which is the root of the key
hierarchy in `blueprint/core.md` — every scope seed below it. Rotation cannot help, because the
attacker holds the root rather than a scope.

#913 capped the window at 8h, which is the only control there is today.

## Work

Hand Core Kit an `IAsyncStorage` wrapper rather than `window.localStorage` directly. `AsyncStorage`
awaits both `getItem` and `setItem`, so an AES-GCM wrapper drops in:

- Generate the wrapping key with `extractable: false` and keep it in IndexedDB. `crypto.subtle`
  will use it in-page and never hand its bytes to script, so a reader of the origin's storage gets
  ciphertext it cannot take off the device.
- Keep the store origin-wide — the failover re-export still needs it (#913).
- Clear the wrapping key on logout, alongside the store teardown #913 added.

That converts a silent offline-replayable theft into an attack that has to stay resident in a live

You are right that it needs reasoning rather than just implementation. Here is where I think the difficulty actually sits, which is what I sent the agent to settle:

**The mechanism may not drop in as cleanly as the issue assumes.** The issue's premise is that `AsyncStorage` awaits both `getItem` and `setItem`, so an AES-GCM wrapper substitutes transparently. **There may be a much cheaper mitigation sitting next to it.** The SessionManager is built with no `allowedOrigin`. If that binding is enforced by the Web3Auth session service rather than only in-page, setting it would blunt the offline-replay-from-any-origin property directly, which is the part that makes this severe. That would not replace #1175, but it would change its urgency and possibly ship in a fraction of the effort.

**The UX cost you are pointing at is real, and it is mostly a desynchronisation problem.** The wrapping key would live in IndexedDB while the store lives in localStorage, and those have different eviction rules — Safari's 7-day ITP eviction, storage-pressure eviction, partial site-data clearing. Every one of those produces a present-but-undecryptable store. The design has to define that as "no session, clear both, front door", fail-closed, and the honest cost is that some users get signed out where today they would not. Wrapping the store makes session persistence strictly less durable. That is the trade to decide deliberately rather than discover.

There is also a correctness trap: two tabs cold-starting concurrently can both generate a wrapping key, and the loser's ciphertext becomes permanently undecryptable. That needs an atomic get-or-create, and it interacts with tab leadership and `promote`.

Worth being clear about the ceiling, too: this does not stop an in-page attacker. They can still decrypt in the live tab and still call `_UNSAFE_exportTssKey()` directly. What it buys is that theft can no longer be silent and offline — it has to stay resident. That is a genuine gain, but it is narrower than "seal the store" sounds.

## Q1 — Does an async storage wrapper drop in? **Yes on the SDK side. No on ours, without changes.**

| `«ck»/dist/lib.esm/mpcCoreKit.js` | call | awaited |
|---|---|---|
| `:78` | `new AsyncStorage(this._storageBaseKey, options.storage)` | constructor, no I/O |

| `:788` | `await this.currentStorage.set('sessionId','')` in `logout()` | yes (comment `:787` says "to accommodate async storage") |
| `:852` / `:859` | `setDeviceFactor` / `getDeviceFactor` | yes |
| `:1171` | `await this.currentStorage.set('sessionId', …)` in `createSession()` | yes |

No sync fast-path, no direct `localStorage[key]`, no `store[key]` read. Constructor `:56-85`, `init()` `:174-252`, `commitChanges()` `:818-833` (remote metadata only), `logout()` `:782-794`, `resetState()` `:1305-1313` (in-memory only, never nulls `currentStorage`), `_UNSAFE_exportTssKey` `:871` — all clean. `this.storageLayer` (`:34,197,205,1309`) is the *remote* `TorusStorageLayer`, unrelated.

**Where it breaks: our own code, landed by #1174.**
- `apps/web/src/auth/coreKit.ts:37` types the field `private readonly store: Storage` and `:91-93` does a **synchronous** `this.store.removeItem(this.coreKit._storageKey)`. Called from three places: `logout()` `:82`, the REQUIRED_SHARE rollback `:64`. An `IAsyncStorage` wrapper has no `removeItem` and no sync surface — `clearStore` must become `Promise<void>` and the field must stop being `Storage`.

## Q2 — `allowedOrigin`: real, server-enforced, but **not reachable** through mpc-core-kit 3.5.0

**It is not plumbed through.** `«ck»/dist/lib.esm/mpcCoreKit.js:79-82`:
```js
this.sessionManager = new SessionManager({ sessionTime: options.sessionTime });
```
`sessionTime` is the only option passed. `allowedOrigin` has **zero** occurrences in `«ck»/dist/lib.esm/*.js` and `«ck»/dist/types/` (options list at `interfaces.d.ts:296-306`). So today the session is always created with the default.
